images.fileTitle: Yellowstone National Park (WY, USA), Grand Prismatic Spring -- 2022 -- 2514.jpg
images.description: Grand Prismatic Spring , Yellowstone National Park , Wyoming , USA Yellowstone National Park was founded on March 1, 1872, and is considered the world’s first national park. It is located primarily in the state of Wyoming, but also extends into Montana and Idaho . The initiative to establish the park was based on scientific expeditions from 1869 to 1871, which documented the unique landscape. President Ulysses S. Grant signed the protection law. The park covers approximately 8,983 km² and is located on a massive volcanic hotspot. About half of all geysers worldwide are found here. The Old Faithful geyser, which erupts approximately every 90 minutes, is famous. In addition to geysers, hot springs, mud pots, and the colorful Grand Prismatic Spring characterize the area. Yellowstone is also an important wildlife refuge. Since the reintroduction of wolves in 1995, it has been considered a model project for nature conservation. The park attracts several million visitors annually and has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1978.
images.alt: Old Faithful Yellowstone — Yellowstone National Park (WY, USA), Grand Prismatic Spring -- 2022 -- 2514.jpg

images.description: <a href=" http://whc.unesco.org/en/list/948 " rel="nofollow">Hoi An Ancient town</a> is located in Viet Nam’s central Quang Nam Province, on the north bank near the mouth of the Thu Bon River. It is an exceptionally well-preserved example of a small-scale trading port active the 15th to 19th centuries which traded widely, both with the countries of Southeast and East Asia and with the rest of the world. Its decline in the later 19th century ensured that it has retained its traditional urban tissue to a remarkable degree. The town reflects a fusion of indigenous and foreign cultures (principally Chinese and Japanese with later European influences) that combined to produce this unique survival. Source: <a href=" http://whc.unesco.org/en/list/948 " rel="nofollow">whc.unesco.org</a> - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - <a href=" https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Vietnam " rel="nofollow">Vietnam</a> , officially the <a href=" https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Vietnam " rel="nofollow">Socialist Republic of Vietnam</a> , is the easternmost country on the Indochina Peninsula in Southeast Asia. With an estimated 94.6 million inhabitants as of 2016, it is the world's 14th-most-populous country, and the ninth-most-populous Asian country. <a href=" https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Vietnam " rel="nofollow">Vietnam</a> is bordered by China to the north, Laos to the northwest, Cambodia to the southwest, Thailand across the Gulf of Thailand to the southwest, and the Philippines, Malaysia and Indonesia across the South China Sea to the east and southeast. Its capital city has been Hanoi since the reunification of North and South <a href=" https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Vietnam " rel="nofollow">Vietnam</a> in 1976, with Ho Chi Minh City as a historical city as well. Source: <a href=" https://www.wikiwand.com/en/Vietnam " rel="nofollow">www.wikiwand.com</a>

images.fileTitle: Mesmerizing colors and grace while witnessing this Traditional Buddhist Mask Dance at the Black-necked Crane Festival, Gangte Monastery, Phobjikha Valley, Bhutan.jpg
images.description: BLACK NECKED CRANE FESTIVAL The annual Black-Necked Crane festival is celebrated at the courtyard of Gangtey Goenpa in Phobjikha valley. The festival is an occasion for the locals to rejoice and celebrate the arrival of this endangered and majestic bird which becomes an inseparable part in their daily lives during the winter months. The annual blacknecked crane festival is organized to generate awareness and understanding on the importance of conserving the endangered Black-Necked Cranes. The festival includes cultural programs such as folk songs and dances (some with black-necked crane themes) and mask dances performed by the local people, crane dances and environmental conservation-themed dramas and songs by school children.

images.fileTitle: PERIYAR NATIONAL PARK AND TIGER RESERVE, THEKKADY, KERALA, INDIA 03.jpg
images.description: The enclosed image is of Periyar National Park, Kerala, India. It can be categorized under the ‘Tiger reserves in India’ and ‘National parks of India’. Periyar National Park and Tiger Reserve, Thekkady, Kerala is a gift of nature in the God’s own country, Kerala. It is a protected area sprawling over an area of about 900 sq km and a home for many rare and endangered flora and fauna. It forms the major watershed of the two important rivers, the Periyar and the Pamba. It is located high in the mountain region of Cardamom hills in the southern Western Ghats along the borders of Tamil Nadu. It is notable as an elephant reserve and tiger reserve. The topography consists of steep and rolling hills which are thickly wooded. The sanctuary surrounds the Periyar Lake, a reservoir measuring 26 sq km which was formed when the Mullaperiyar Dam was erected in 1895. Humid climate prevails here. Temperature varies from 12°C in winter to 35°C in summer. The park consists of Tropical evergreen and moist deciduous type forest. There are different species of floras flowering plants, orchids and grass. Around 33 species of mammals are recorded to dwell here which include Bengal tigers, gaurs, Indian elephants, wild pig, jungle cat, Nilgiri martens etc. Hundreds of species of reptiles, birds, insects are also found here. The enclosed image is of the wild pigs in the Periyar forest.

images.fileTitle: PERIYAR NATIONAL PARK AND TIGER RESERVE, THEKKADY, KERALA, INDIA 03.jpg
images.description: The enclosed image is of Periyar National Park, Kerala, India. It can be categorized under the ‘Tiger reserves in India’ and ‘National parks of India’. Periyar National Park and Tiger Reserve, Thekkady, Kerala is a gift of nature in the God’s own country, Kerala. It is a protected area sprawling over an area of about 900 sq km and a home for many rare and endangered flora and fauna. It forms the major watershed of the two important rivers, the Periyar and the Pamba. It is located high in the mountain region of Cardamom hills in the southern Western Ghats along the borders of Tamil Nadu. It is notable as an elephant reserve and tiger reserve. The topography consists of steep and rolling hills which are thickly wooded. The sanctuary surrounds the Periyar Lake, a reservoir measuring 26 sq km which was formed when the Mullaperiyar Dam was erected in 1895. Humid climate prevails here. Temperature varies from 12°C in winter to 35°C in summer. The park consists of Tropical evergreen and moist deciduous type forest. There are different species of floras flowering plants, orchids and grass. Around 33 species of mammals are recorded to dwell here which include Bengal tigers, gaurs, Indian elephants, wild pig, jungle cat, Nilgiri martens etc. Hundreds of species of reptiles, birds, insects are also found here. The enclosed image is of the wild pigs in the Periyar forest.
